q: An inertial manifold for a dissipative PDE is a finite-dimensional invariant manifold that:
opts: Is defined only for linear PDEs
exp: An inertial manifold (Foias–Sell–Temam, 1988) is a finite-dimensional positively invariant Lipschitz manifold that attracts all trajectories exponentially. Its existence justifies finite-dimensional reduction of infinite-dimensional PDEs.
